what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/audio-transcription: hearing a recording or a link's video into timed words on the person's computer (computer rows), and the audio-transcription package's own local Whisper transcription with word times, plus finding where Whisper looped and hearing only those windows again.

payload.label: Transcribe a recording with a time for every word, and repair Whisper loops (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Turn a recording into a transcript with a time for every word, and fix the places where the transcription got stuck repeating one sentence
payload.description: Runs the audio-transcription package's own transcribe-audio.py on the person's own computer: the recording (audio, or video with sound) is decoded to 16 kHz mono and read by whisper.cpp, and the answer is the package's result: language, full text, segments, and words with a start, an end and a timing_source that says whether the time came from the engine's token times, from the segment's bounds or from an even split of the segment. The seam adds the recording's length, its path, and when it was made (a camera's sidecar XML beside it, else the file's time). transcribe-many does a whole folder, skipping recordings already done, a few at once and waiting while the computer is busy. Whisper sometimes gets stuck and writes one sentence again and again over minutes of real speech or silence. find-loops finds those stretches (a sentence said four or more times that fills half a segment, or a segment that repeats the one before). repair merges the ones that are close, hears again only those windows with the earlier text not carried in (whisper.cpp -mc 0) and splices the new words in at their true seconds. A sentence that still loops is taken out and kept in removed_hallucinated, so nothing disappears silently; repair-many repairs a whole folder, each transcript from the recording it names. judge says whether a whole answer is to be trusted at all (one segment said over and over, one run of four words coming back again and again, too few different words, too few words a minute, mostly no speech) and why. index writes one line per transcript (length, words, segments, first thing said) with the totals, and text writes a transcript as [m:ss] paragraphs about thirty seconds long (with the title and header lines the person gives), refusing one judge rejects. When a transcript does not carry its recording's length, judge and text take it as --duration, or judge takes each recording's length from a tab-separated list (--durations). Nothing leaves the computer and no key is needed.

input.description: The recording on the person's computer, put where {input} is in the command.

output.description: The JSON file to write the transcript to, put where {output} is in the command.

output_schema.description: The last line each command prints: {"result": ...}. transcribe: {transcript, segments, words, duration, language}, or {failed: {code, message}} with exit 2. find-loops: {transcripts_with_loops: [{transcript, segments, seconds}], total_looped_seconds}. repair: {transcript, repaired_windows, removed}, or clean or skipped. transcribe-many: {recordings: [{recording, transcript, status}], ok, skipped, failed}. repair-many: {transcripts: [{transcript, status}]}. judge: {verdicts: [{transcript, accepted, reasons}], rejected}. index: {index, recordings, hours, silent, segments, words}. text: {text, paragraphs}, or {refused, reasons} with exit 2.

needs: a ggml Whisper model file, named in --model-path (for example ggml-tiny.en.bin, or a larger one from the whisper.cpp project for better words)
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion. If you can run commands where they are: check that whisper-cli and ffmpeg are installed (get_it has the commands) and ask which ggml model file to use, then run `run` with their recording in place of {input}, a new .json file for {output} and the model file for MODEL.bin. Then run the same script with `find-loops --transcript {output}` and tell the person which stretches looped and for how many seconds. If any did, run it with `repair --transcript {output} --audio {input} --model-path MODEL.bin`, then run find-loops again to show that the loops are gone. Tell the person each word's timing_source, because words timed by an even split of a segment are estimates. For a whole folder of recordings use `transcribe-many --recordings FOLDER --out-dir FOLDER --model-path MODEL.bin` (add --pattern for the files, --workers to hear a few at once, --max-load to wait while the computer is busy), then `repair-many --transcript FOLDER/*.json --model-path MODEL.bin` and `index --transcripts FOLDER`. Run `judge --transcript FILE` before trusting a transcript, and tell the person any it rejects and why; `text --transcript FILE --out FILE.txt` writes a readable [m:ss] transcript from one it accepts. If a command fails, its last line says the code and why. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: The audio-transcription package's transcribe-audio.py (copied unchanged), run with whisper.cpp (MIT, https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp) and ffmpeg

payload.label: Read transcript and caption files into timed words, and check quotes against them (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Read a folder of transcript files (srt, vtt, txt, json) or a channel's downloaded YouTube captions into one timed-words shape, and check that quotes really are in the transcripts at the times they cite
payload.description: Five readers on the person's own computer, none of which hears audio or reads the network. pick_transcript_files.py picks, from an asset index (JSON lines with root, ext, name, display_path, sha256), the files of one drive or library that look like transcripts (srt or vtt, or a name with transcript, _raw., _clean., _cleaned_up or _rag.), names each one's kind, and joins each to the person's file store by its sha256 (the files door's answer given as a JSON file, or a namespace sqlite copy opened read only), listing one the store does not hold as missing. read_transcript_files.py reads each listed file's bytes (or one file) into a words.json: srt and vtt cues, '## h:mm:ss.fff - h:mm:ss.fff' txt blocks with their source line, 'hh:mm:ss:ff' timecode txt at the frames per second given, or a recognizer's json with its words; it says whether the timing is per word, per segment or none, and keeps the whole text of a file with no times. caption_transcripts.py turns a channel download (raw/json3 caption files, raw/meta and raw/flat-videos.jsonl, as yt-dlp leaves them for tool:keep-channels-latest-videos-and-captions) into one [m:ss] paragraph transcript per video, preferring a video's manual English track, and an index of every listed video. find_whisper_quotes.py checks each quote cited from a whisper transcript: it finds the quote's exact words among the word times and says whether it starts inside the cited window. show_segments.py prints a transcript's segments between two seconds. Each prints its account and a last line {"result": ...}.

input.description: The transcript file, list or folder on the person's computer, put where {input} is in the command.

output.description: The file or folder to write, put where {output} is in the command.

output_schema.description: The last line each command prints: {"result": ...}. read_transcript_files.py read-file: {words_json, timing, segments, words, duration}; read-files: {written, already_read, not_in_files, by_format_and_timing}. pick_transcript_files.py: {files, list, by_kind_and_origin}. caption_transcripts.py: {rows, with_captions, index}. find_whisper_quotes.py: {quotes, problems, hits: [{video, stamp, quote, found, start, end, in_window, hit, of}]}. show_segments.py: {segments: [{start, text}]}.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion. For one transcript file run `run` with the file in place of {input} and a new .words.json for {output}. For a drive's transcripts: ask for the asset index file, the drive's root name and the store (the files door's answer saved as JSON, or a namespace sqlite copy), run `pick_transcript_files.py --assets FILE --root NAME --held FILE --out LIST.tsv`, then, once the listed files' bytes are in a folder as <hex>.<ext>, `read_transcript_files.py read-files --list LIST.tsv --bytes FOLDER --out-dir FOLDER --root NAME --origin STORE` (add --fps for timecode transcripts not at 24 frames a second). For a channel downloaded with yt-dlp: `caption_transcripts.py --corpus FOLDER --channel LABEL`; for videos with no captions use tool:hear-a-link, then audio_transcription.py judge and text. Before trusting quotes taken from whisper transcripts run `find_whisper_quotes.py --corpus FOLDER` and tell the person every quote not found or outside its window. `show_segments.py FILE START END` shows what was said between two seconds. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: Moved from Trillion-X/trillion-launch-video tools/ (the drive transcript-file parser and picker, the channel caption builder, the whisper quote audit and the segment printer); ports/ names each source

payload.label: Hear a recording into timed words on my computer
payload.job: Turn a recording in my files into its words with times, heard free on my own computer
payload.description: Reads a recording from the person's files (`file`, its name or identity) through the run's door into the run's own folder, hears it with the whisper-cli and ggml model the person granted (do-work/audio_transcription.py transcribe), and answers text, timed segments and language. The copy is removed once heard; the person's file is never changed. Nothing is sent to a paid speech service.

file.description: The recording's name or identity in the person's files
file.x-free-text-because: A file name in the person's files.

model_path.description: The ggml Whisper model file on this computer, in the models folder the person granted
model_path.x-free-text-because: A file path on this computer.

whisper_cli.description: The whisper-cli program the person granted (default: the one on PATH)
whisper_cli.x-free-text-because: A file path on this computer.

ffmpeg.description: The ffmpeg program the person granted (default: the one on PATH)
ffmpeg.x-free-text-because: A file path on this computer.

language.description: The language spoken, when known (for example en)

stand_in_programs.whisper-cli:
base=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do [ "$1" = "-of" ] && base="$2"; shift; done
cat > "$base.json" <<'JSON'
{"result":{"language":"en"},"transcription":[{"offsets":{"from":0,"to":2500},"text":" Welcome to the sample meeting, said Ada Example."},{"offsets":{"from":2500,"to":5000},"text":" The next item is the garden budget."}]}
JSON
stand_in_programs.ffmpeg:
last=""; decode=0
for a in "$@"; do last="$a"; [ "$a" = "-y" ] && decode=1; done
if [ "$decode" = 1 ]; then printf 'RIFF' > "$last"; else echo "  Duration: 00:00:05.00, start: 0.000000, bitrate: 256 kb/s" >&2; fi

provenance.source: audio-transcription/read-data/hear-here.mjs, moved from the product repo's computer/listen.mjs and computer/hear-a-link.mjs

payload.label: Hear the words of a video or recording at a link
payload.job: Get the words said in a video or recording at a link, from its captions or heard on my own computer
payload.description: Reads the page at `url` with the link reader the person has (read-data/hear-a-link.json fetchers, such as yt-dlp; `link_reader` names its program). The page's own captions win when it has them; otherwise its sound is fetched and heard with the whisper-cli and ggml model the person granted. The heard sound is kept in the person's files (/Heard links, named by the page's title) with its words beside it, unless keep_sound is false. A link with no words always fails with why. Nothing is kept on the computer after the run.

url.description: The link to a video or a recording

languages.description: Caption languages to ask for, in the link reader's words (default en.*,en)

link_reader.description: The link reader program (such as yt-dlp) on this computer
link_reader.x-free-text-because: A file path on this computer.

keep_sound.description: Keep the heard sound in the person's files (default true)

model_path.description: The ggml Whisper model file on this computer, in the models folder the person granted
model_path.x-free-text-because: A file path on this computer.

whisper_cli.description: The whisper-cli program the person granted (default: the one on PATH)
whisper_cli.x-free-text-because: A file path on this computer.

ffmpeg.description: The ffmpeg program the person granted (default: the one on PATH)
ffmpeg.x-free-text-because: A file path on this computer.

language.description: The language spoken, when known (for example en)

stand_in_programs.yt-dlp:
folder=""; out=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do [ "$1" = "-o" ] && out="$2"; [ "$1" = "--dump-single-json" ] && info=1; shift; done
if [ -n "$info" ]; then echo '{"title": "Sample garden talk", "duration": 12.5}'; exit 0; fi
folder=$(dirname "$out")
printf 'WEBVTT

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:02.500
Welcome to the sample garden talk.

00:00:02.500 --> 00:00:05.000
Today we plant tomatoes.
' > "$folder/captions.en.vtt"

provenance.source: audio-transcription/read-data/hear-here.mjs, moved from the product repo's computer/listen.mjs and computer/hear-a-link.mjs

payload.label: Time each word of a voice take from where the voice really starts, for graphics on the word (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Make the word times of my voice take start where each word is actually heard, so on-screen graphics land on the word and not early in the pause before it
payload.description: Reads a voice take and its word times (a Whisper word list) and moves each word's start to the first 10 ms window inside the word whose level is above a silence line (default -45 dBFS); each end stays. Whisper puts part of a pause into the next word's start, so a graphic timed to it lands early. Given the take's line file (its script), each word takes the script's spelling when the script and Whisper give the same number of words, and a word Whisper split at a hyphen is joined into one; otherwise Whisper's spelling stays and the answer says why. Writes {source, timing, words: [{text, start, end}]} and answers how many words moved.

request.description: The request JSON file, put where {request} is in the command: {take, words, out, line?, edge_db?}.

output_schema.description: Last line {"result": {"out", "words", "moved", "spelling"}}, or {"error": "what to change"} with exit 2.

needs: the voice take and its Whisper word times
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer. Hear the take first (tool:transcribe-audio-and-repair-whisper-loops or whisper_here) for its word times, then write the request with the take, those words, the take's line file if there is one, and a new output file. Read the last line: how many words moved and whose spelling the words carry. Time graphics from the output, never from the raw Whisper starts.

provenance.source: Moved from a film repository's films/<film>/narrator/tools/word_onsets.py; the silence line is a request field
